summary: Critical security issue detected: a hardcoded AWS access key was found in src/services/StorageService.cs. Additionally, a missing authorization check on PUT /api/users/{id} violates OWASP A01. Code-quality and architecture findings are advisory.
recommendations: Remove the hardcoded AWS access key from src/services/StorageService.cs and load it from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID environment variable or AWS Secrets Manager.
Add an authorization attribute ([Authorize(Roles="Admin")]) to UserController.Update.
Refactor OrderProcessor.CalculateTotals (cyclomatic complexity 14) into smaller helpers.
Add unit tests for PaymentService.Refund covering the partial-refund edge case.
Move NotificationService.SendEmail out of the Domain layer; it imports MailKit, violating layering rules.

security.description: AWS access key embedded in source. Pattern matched: AKIA prefix.
security.remediation: Rotate the key immediately, then load from environment or AWS Secrets Manager.

security.description: Missing authorization check on PUT /api/users/{id} — any authenticated user can update any other user.
security.remediation: Add [Authorize(Policy="OwnerOrAdmin")] and verify the caller owns the resource.

code_quality.suggestion: Extract tax, discount, and shipping calculations into separate methods.
Extract to a shared IValidator<T> implementation.

code_quality.description: Variable 'd' used for discount amount — non-descriptive.

testing.description: No tests exist for PaymentService.Refund covering partial refunds.
testing.recommendation: Add tests for: full refund, partial refund, refund exceeding original amount.

architecture.description: NotificationService in Domain imports MailKit — infrastructure leakage.
architecture.remediation: Move NotificationService to Infrastructure; inject an INotificationSender port into the domain.
